timeline.text: With 195+ outlets across India, Canada, the USA, and Australia, Jay Bhavani aims to exceed 200 by March 2025 while expanding into the UK and New Zealand. Its Export Division has shipped 50+ reefer containers globally.

Jay Bhavani entered the USA in May 2023 and now operates 8 outlets, with more coming soon. Evolving beyond Vadapav, Jay Bhavani serves diverse South and North Indian fast-food delicacies, delighting customers with authentic flavors.

Inspired by the café trend, Mr. Kishansingh Rajput launched premium Jay Bhavani outlets in January 2022 under "Jay Bhavani Snacks Bar & Café" in Ahmedabad. Jay Bhavani's Canada success led to its first Australian outlet in Canberra by December 2022.
Amidst the global challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, Jay Bhavani marked a significant milestone in October 2021 by opening its first international outlet in Etobicoke, Toronto, Canada.
The COVID-19 pandemic caused Jay Bhavani to drop below the 150-outlet mark, but the brand resiliently bounced back, breaking boundaries beyond India to embark on its international journey.
Jay Bhavani Vadapav had surpassed the 151-outlet milestone and was rapidly expanding.
Jay Bhavani Vadapav ventured beyond Gujarat by opening its first out-of-state outlet, marking its 101st location in Udaipur, Rajasthan.
A team of professionals joined forces to propel the Jay Bhavani Vadapav brand to new heights.

The year 2014 marked a significant milestone for Jay Bhavani Vadapav, as the company took its first big leap by transitioning its company-owned outlet in Palanpur to a franchise for the very first time.
Following the resounding success of the Anandnagar outlet, Jay Bhavani expanded further by opening four additional outlets in Bopal, Bodakdev, Vastrapur, and Gurukul.
Among four brothers, Mr. Kishan Singh Rajput opened his own outlet in Anand Nagar, a move that made history and played a pivotal role in building the brand to the renowned level it enjoys today.
What began as a roadside cart evolved into the opening of Jay Bhavani Vadapav’s first outlet near GLS College in Ahmedabad, marking the start of a never-ending journey for the brand.
Adopted a business strategy by acquiring the vadapav business van of a competitor who had set up right across from their location.
In the spring of 1998, Jay Bhavani first opened their food cart at Municipal Market, C.G.Road, Ahmedabad, with a capital investment of Rs. 5,000, where they sold Vadapav at Rs.4 per piece.
